legacy_skills.name: advisor-planner
legacy_skills.notes: Historical v2 migration record only. The folder is removed; do not reintroduce it as a live alias or stub.

incompatible_changes.detail: v2 'next_skill' (a single ambiguous pointer) is forbidden in skill-team/v3. It is replaced by 'required_skill' (the only skill allowed to run now) and 'successor_skill' (the skill expected after the current handoff is validated and consumed).
incompatible_changes.migration: migrate_v2_to_v3.py infers required_skill and successor_skill from the v2 stage/status pair using a documented heuristic table, and never leaves next_skill in migrated output.

incompatible_changes.detail: 'planning-delegation/v2' becomes 'skill-team/v3' on every migrated frontmatter block (PROGRESS.md and handoffs).
incompatible_changes.migration: migrate_v2_to_v3.py rewrites the field on every YAML frontmatter block it touches.

incompatible_changes.detail: v2 ended at ROUTING with an implicit, unowned implementation step. skill-team/v3 adds an explicit IMPLEMENTATION stage owned by 'execute-routed-task', with its own statuses (TASK_IN_PROGRESS, TASK_BLOCKED, TASK_COMPLETE, IMPLEMENTATION_COMPLETE).
incompatible_changes.migration: Projects with v2 status IMPLEMENTATION_READY or later map to stage: IMPLEMENTATION, status: TASK_IN_PROGRESS (or IMPLEMENTATION_COMPLETE when v2 records show all tasks done); required_skill: execute-routed-task.

incompatible_changes.detail: v2 had no formal, independent review stage. skill-team/v3 adds REVIEW owned by 'review-implementation-evidence', gating release on REVIEW_APPROVED.
incompatible_changes.migration: Not inferable from v2 data; migrated projects land with review_revision: 0 and require a first pass through review-implementation-evidence before release.

incompatible_changes.detail: v2 had no formal release gate. skill-team/v3 adds RELEASE owned by 'validate-release-readiness', with RELEASE_READY / RELEASED / POST_RELEASE_REVIEW_REQUIRED statuses.
incompatible_changes.migration: Migrated projects land with release_revision: 0 and required_skill left at the correctly inferred earlier stage; release is never auto-approved by the migrator.

incompatible_changes.detail: v2 treated discovery as a single implicit step (often folded into advisor-planner or an unnamed brainstorm). skill-team/v3 defines three non-competing discovery owners: brainstorm-idea-with-user (intent), investigate-existing-codebase (technical reality), product-ux-audit (rendered UI/UX).
incompatible_changes.migration: migrate_v2_to_v3.py does not guess which discovery mode a v2 project used; it records DISCOVERY with stage_owner left for manual confirmation when ambiguous, and never invents a value.

incompatible_changes.detail: v2 tracked plan_revision and routing_revision only. skill-team/v3 requires discovery_revision, plan_revision, routing_revision, implementation_revision, review_revision, release_revision as a full monotonic set.
incompatible_changes.migration: migrate_v2_to_v3.py adds any missing *_revision field with a default of 0 and never decreases an existing value.

incompatible_changes.detail: v2 used NOT_READY/READY. skill-team/v3 adds CONSUMED to mark a handoff a downstream skill has already read and acted on, distinct from a stale but still-READY handoff.
incompatible_changes.migration: migrate_v2_to_v3.py leaves READY handoffs as READY; it does not infer CONSUMED without explicit evidence of downstream consumption.

incompatible_changes.detail: v2 had no explicit write-lock field. skill-team/v3 requires writer_skill (and writer_task) so only one skill holds operational write authorization at a time.
incompatible_changes.migration: migrate_v2_to_v3.py adds writer_skill: null and writer_task: null when absent, on the assumption that no writer is currently mid-operation.

incompatible_changes.detail: skill-team/v3 requires English-only IDs, states, schema fields, and contracts. Legacy Portuguese aliases (e.g. PENDENTE, EM_ANDAMENTO, CONCLUIDA) belong only inside the migrator, never in new artifacts.
incompatible_changes.migration: migrate_v2_to_v3.py maps known Portuguese/legacy state aliases to the English vocabulary and reports any alias it cannot map instead of guessing.

platform_notes.core_contract: The workflow contract, SKILL.md files, catalog/*.json, contracts/*.md, and all scripts/*.py are platform-neutral: plain Markdown, flat YAML frontmatter, and Python 3.10+ stdlib only. Any agent runtime that can read local files and run Python can operate the pipeline.

adapters.codex: Optional installation guidance only. Codex consumes the portable SKILL.md core and must follow the consumer project's canonical PROGRESS.md.
adapters.opencode: Optional installation guidance only. OpenCode consumes the portable SKILL.md core; agents/*.yaml is supplementary metadata and never behavioral authority.
adapters.cursor: Optional installation guidance only. Cursor may expose SKILL.md through its discovery mechanism; it must use the same canonical paths, pointer, and validators as every other harness.
adapters.note: The 'openai.yaml' filename under each skill's agents/ folder is legacy generic interface metadata. It is optional and additive; adapters must not duplicate state, add core dependencies, or contradict SKILL.md and contracts/skill-team-v3.md.
